podcast.title: Donna's Domain Review
podcast.body: Goldfinger guitarist Charlie Paulson "apparently lacks rhythm" according to a review on Donna's Domain, a website that rates rock stars' penis size and sexual ability. This critique specifically targets his musical attribute in the context of the website's evaluations. "And Goldfinger guitarist Charlie Palson apparently lacks rhythm."

podcast.title: Influence from Fishbone
podcast.body: Goldfinger is among the bands that have cited Fishbone as an important influence on their music. "Goldfinger."

podcast.title: Mid-to-Late 90s Success
podcast.body: Goldfinger enjoyed a successful run during the middle and late 1990s, gaining considerable radio play for their songs and significant exposure through music video channels such as MTV. "Gold finger, a group had a really good run in the middle and late 90s. Lots of radio play for songs like that and lots of exposure thanks to video channels in MTV."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Success Following The Offspring
podcast.body: This band was discovered by fans due to The Offspring's significant success in late 1994, marking the beginning of Skate Punk's "glory years." "And this led to fans discovering bands like Goldfinger, Lagwagon, Face to Face, MXPX, and Unwritten Law."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Wave Ska Band
podcast.body: Goldfinger was identified as a band from the "third wave" of Ska, which arrived in the 1990s. This wave saw significant popularity with bands like No Doubt, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, Reel Big Fish, and Dance Hall Crashers. "Third wave Scott arrived in the 1990s, no doubt, muddy, muddy boss tones, sublime, real big fish, gold finger, dancehall crashes and so many more."

podcast.title: Warped Tour Feature
podcast.body: Goldfinger was one of the bands featured during the initial years of the Warped Tour, a key platform for pop punk and ska punk music. "In just the first few years, the tour featured bad religion, dancehall crashes, face to face, bucket nine, less than Jake, muddy, muddy boss tones, no doubt, sublime, and gold finger."

xref.title: First Multi-Bond Theme Singer
xref.body: Shirley Bassey was the first artist to sing multiple James Bond themes, starting with "Goldfinger" in 1964. She later returned for "Diamonds Are Forever" in 1971 and "Moonraker" in 1979, establishing a recurring presence in the franchise's musical history. "It would also be the first of three Shirley Bassie Bond themes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Founding Her Own Studio for New Sounds
xref.body: After leaving the BBC in 1959, Daphne Oram established her own studio devoted to creating new electronic sounds. Her work there extended to film, where she produced all the electronic sound effects for the first three James Bond movies: "Dr. No," "From Russia with Love," and "Goldfinger," showcasing her unique sonic artistry. "When she left the Beebe in 1959, she founded her own studio devoted to creating new sounds."

xref.body: Fishbone holds a fanatical following and is cited as an important influence by a long list of bands, including Sublime, 311, Goldfinger, Rage Against the Machine, and Faith No More. "No doubt. Sublime. 311. Goldfinger. Rage Against The Machine. Faith No More."

xref.title: James Bond Electronic Sounds
xref.body: Daphne Oram was responsible for creating the distinctive electronic sounds heard in three James Bond movies: *Dr. No*, *From Russia with Love*, and *Goldfinger*. "For example, the electronic sounds you hear in three James Bond movies, Dr. No from Russia with Love and Goldfinger, were all created by Daphne Orham."

xref.body: No Doubt was a prominent band in the "third wave" of Ska, which arrived in the 1990s. This wave saw significant popularity with bands like The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, Reel Big Fish, Goldfinger, and Dance Hall Crashers. The Interrupters were noted as the first female-fronted Ska band to have a major hit since No Doubt. "Third wave Scott arrived in the 1990s, no doubt, muddy, muddy boss tones, sublime, real big fish, gold finger, dancehall crashes and so many more." "They became the first female fronted Skaban to have a major hit since no doubt."
